sections.text:
Track 1: skip the boot-time structural walk via a WALK_VERIFIED_TIP checkpoint (issue #6)
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
This pull request is merged.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/16

Track 1 of #6. Follows the converged design in that thread (maintainer greenlit "open Track 1's PR whenever ready").

## Motivation

Phase 3a (#9) made boot fast by persisting the UTXO snapshot, but the live-node measurement in #6 showed boot is two roughly-equal halves: the snapshot load + SMT rebuild, **and** `open_chain`'s structural per-block walk. At height 638,569 the walk alone was **~22s** — every boot re-reads every canonical block body and re-runs `validate_block_header*` + cumulative-work derivation over blocks that were already validated when first received.

This PR removes that half for a healthy node. It is **not** a constant-time open — on a stale or legacy datadir the walk still runs (partially or fully). It skips the walk only when a marker proves it was already done through the current tip.

## Design

A new `WALK_VERIFIED_TIP` marker in `META_TABLE`, advanced in lockstep with `TIP_KEY` by every atomic commit — exactly mirroring the `UTXO_SNAPSHOT_TIP` lifecycle, with **one deliberate difference: no `COMPLETE` gate**. A block only reaches `commit_block_atomic`/`commit_reorg_atomic` after full validation, so stamping "structurally verified through this tip" is always truthful, even on a legacy datadir.

`open_chain` becomes a three-state decision (same shape as the snapshot-marker branch above it):

| marker vs tip | action |
|---|---|
| `== tip` | **skip the walk**; read cumulative work O(1) from `WORK_TABLE` (defensive fall-through to full walk if absent) |
| stale ancestor | **partial walk** of the suffix `[marker_height+1 ..= tip]` only |
| absent | **full walk** (legacy / post-`--rebuild-state` / post-`--full-verify`), then stamp the marker |

Lifecycle wiring: `commit_genesis_atomic` seeds it; `commit_block_atomic`/`commit_reorg_atomic` advance it in the same `write_txn` as `TIP_KEY` (crash-before-commit rolls back, so it never references an orphaned hash); `finalize_utxo_snapshot` stamps it (replay ⊇ walk); `clear_utxo_snapshot` drops it.

## Trust model (called out explicitly)

Skipping the walk relaxes corruption detection: header-linkage / block-body / tx-root / coinbase-shape corruption in **old canonical blocks** becomes a latent runtime failure (surfaced when that block is next read, e.g. a reorg back through it) instead of a boot-time abort. Acceptable for routine operation — old canonical blocks are immutable and were validated on arrival — and the new **`--full-verify`** flag forces a one-shot full walk for defense-in-depth, re-stamping the marker so the next boot is fast again. The persisted-UTXO `state_root` cross-check is unchanged.
